action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

Untapped capability: proposed Ink (live view of a file as Claude writes it, from turn.step input chunks), Courtesy (thanks answered locally by a turn.step hook, no request), Attic (unused tool schemas stowed behind ToolSearch via tool.describe)

Person at the terminal: proposed Outage (a failed network command checked against the provider's status page), Drift (CLAUDE.md claims checked against the tree as the session opens), Usual (how long this command took here before, as a bar while it runs)

Delight: proposed Unsent (what you typed and took back before sending, from prompt.edit, kept only in memory), Understudy (the engine's own guess at your next prompt scored against what you then said), Overheard (the sentences in Claude's thinking summary that are about you)
took the order at ideation
stamped reject on "Ink": It is pen-widget, which WO-0023 already has at inspection: the same file drawn from the same streaming Write and Edit arguments, with only a stop verb added.

stamped reject on "Courtesy": Not chosen: the mechanism is new, but it puts words in the transcript as Claude's that no model wrote, a false match swallows a real instruction, and the tokens it spares are mostly cheap cache reads, so the headline figure overstates the gain.

stamped reject on "Attic": The engine already defers MCP tools behind ToolSearch by itself, ToolInfo carries no schema so the weight it reports is a guess, and each stow spends the prompt cache: too little gained for the cost.

stamped reject on "Drift": A variation on footnotes-widget: the same check of paths and names against the working tree, pointed at CLAUDE.md instead of the reply, and silent for good once the file is fixed.

stamped reject on "Usual": A variation on what exists: activity-widget and checks-widget already time commands and ghost-widget (waiting) already races this project's past runs; it adds only a remembered average.

stamped reject on "Unsent": It puts on a standing card exactly the sentences the person decided not to show, in view of any screen share, for a novelty that fades in a day: the exposure is out of proportion to what it gives.
stamped reject on "Understudy": A variation on wager-widget with the bet turned round: one more prediction score, nothing to act on, and empty wherever prompt suggestions are off.
stamped reject on "Overheard": A variation on premise-widget, as its inventor concedes: the same thinking-summary sentences filtered by a different pattern, and it does nothing with them.
named the widget outage-widget ("Outage")

took the order at build

Note 1: chose the install-like word. npm/pnpm/yarn/bun, pip/pip3/pipx/uv/poetry/twine and cargo name their provider only when the next non-flag word is install-like (install, i, ci, add, update, publish, build for cargo, ...); gh, npx and bunx name theirs alone. So A6's chain 'npm test && git push' with a github.com timeout checks GitHub alone, and both only when the text names npm's host. Notes 2-3: fixed wordings fall to the short form when the wide one does not fit; a stranger falls to 'no page: host', then 'host: none' with the host cut in the middle. Note 4: the elsewhere toast reads 'GitHub reports the incident resolved; another is open elsewhere.' Note 9: an unread check never replaces an open incident, on any path. Note 10: a result already turned to deny is left alone (A15); redact-widget and this do not compose. Also: crates is named crates.io in sentences, toasts and answers; related components are listed first; the lag row needs a report that is not a stranger; a started_at in the future falls through like an unparseable one.

Engine finding: inside a hook that has awaited, read($, isOn) and $.state.get answer with the value from when the hook began, even after a command switched the widget off; update() answers with the current value. The widget re-reads the switch after next(e) and after the fetch with update($, isOn, shown => shown) (lit). redact-widget's second read after next(e) has the same blind spot. The fetch stand-in in tests is a bottom on('http.fetch') hook, not ground()'s answers, because an answer cannot be late. Not type-checked with tsc (none installed); validator, 20 tests and renders pass.

stamped pass: Built outage-widget: a failed Bash or PowerShell network command is matched to GitHub, npm, PyPI or crates.io, the provider's unresolved-incidents page is read within 2 s, the verdict is drawn on the card and one sentence per new related incident is appended to the failed result, with a one-minute poll and toast while an incident is open; 15 acceptance tests and the checker pass.
